text: The three masking-profile operations have no row in the ownership map and none in TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A, whose only access reads are API-P4-007 GET /admin/roles and API-P4-008 GET /admin/access-log. This revision fixes them on the base /api/recovery/access/v1: GET /admin/masking-profiles for the profile read by role and by field with the version in force, POST /admin/masking-profile-versions for the profile version write, and POST /admin/masking-profiles/{roleCode}/unmask for the unmask request and its record. The profile read carries the Reference data right R and the version write the Reference data right C of TSD P4 v3 T6.1; the unmask carries no Reference data letter and is authorised by the unmasked value of the rule in the version in force for one of the caller's roles, with 401 and 403 on the default deny rule.
why: No source fixes the paths or the rights of a masking-profile operation, and the legacy Endpoints table named only the reference-load load and approve operations, which belong to RWB-P4-AD009-APP, RWB-P4-AD010-APP and RWB-P4-E1037-APP.

applied_in: RWB-P4-AD004-APP sections 1, 3, 8 (BR8), 10, 12.1 and 13; RWB-P4-AD004-CON sections 3, 8 (BR8), 12.1 and 13
confirm: Solution architect and API owner at the contract freeze
impact: Medium: the three paths and their rights are the public face of the profile and must be agreed before the app story builds them.

text: The PII log of legacy AC2 is the ACE Common audit and PII Kafka path to the SOC (Architecture v5 slide 20; TSD P4 v3 T5.1 INT-22), not a table of rwb_access. The unmask read is written through the ACE Common logging client; no producer, record name or field list for that record is fixed by any source, so the record shape in section 11 is carried as a placeholder and the app writes no PII table of its own.
why: The legacy criterion requires the read to be written to the PII log and no source places that log in this service or gives it a record; Architecture v5 and TSD P4 v3 hand PII, audit and SOC logging to ACE Common.

text: A personal field is masked by default. A field with no rule in the version in force, or with a rule whose unmasked is false for every role the caller holds, is answered from the masked view column named by its field id, v_ace_customer.id_no_masked (DF-ACE-073) or v_ace_contact.contact_value_masked (DF-ACE-079); where the view holds no masked column, the value is masked by the masker of RWB-PLT-E1037-CON in the form the FSD example fixes, XXXX-XX-XX for a date and XXXXXX5678 for a phone.
why: The legacy criterion and the FSD state that a personal field with no masking rule is masked, and the FSD gives a masked form for a date and a phone but no general rule; the masker is the library that holds one.

text: The access record of a personal-field read is written by the access-entry writer of RWB-P4-E1039-APP through the local decision-record library. This story supplies the masking version label in force, the field ids, their masked flags and the case reference, and writes no access-log row of its own; the same version label is carried on the PII record of an unmask, so both records name the version in force.
why: Legacy AC3 requires the access log to carry the version in force while the access log and its writer belong to RWB-P4-E1039-APP and RWB-P4-AD007-APP, so the version has to travel with the answer rather than be written by this story.

impact: Medium: the version is visible in the access log without a second writer and without an access-log table in this story.

text: The Compliance approval of a masking_rule version is the reference-load approve gate and not this story. The version write stores the rows with their version label and valid_from; the approval is the A decision of RWB-P4-AD010-APP on the reference-load path, with the approver role the parameter rwb.refload.approver.masking_rule names (RW-COMPLY). This story writes no approval state and no load record.
why: Legacy AC3 starts from a version approved by Compliance, and the approve gate is the sibling story's; one criterion cannot be answered twice and masking_rule has no status column to write.

text: A committed masking-profile version is published once as rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1 on rwb.access.events.v1 with change kind MASKING. The write path of this story publishes it in the transaction of the version write through the outbox; where a masking version arrives through the masking-load path of RWB-P4-E1037-APP, that path publishes the same event and the same change kind and this story's writer is not called, so one version is never published twice.
why: Architecture v5 gives this service one access-policy event and this key owns the MASKING publication, while the sibling masking-load path also commits masking versions; one event name and one publisher per committed version keep the cache refresh correct.
read: Architecture v5 slides 14 (rwb.access.events.v1: AccessPolicyChanged, DoaLimitChanged), 20 (consumers refresh their cache on AccessPolicyChanged) and 43 (consumers: all, cache refresh); RWB-P4-E1037-CON section 12.3

confirm: Tech lead of RWB-P4-E1037-APP at the contract freeze
impact: Medium: a second publication of the same version would refresh every cache twice and a missing one would leave a stale profile.

text: masking_rule carries field_id (DF-REF-200, varchar(16)) and no view or column column, so the legacy rule that a masking profile names the view column the masked value comes from is realised as the field id of that view column. The profile answer resolves each field id through the P1 field registry to its view and column (DF-ACE-073 id_no_masked, DF-ACE-074 id_no_last4, DF-ACE-078 contact_value, DF-ACE-079 contact_value_masked), and a field id that is not a personal field of a recovery.v_ace_* view or of a Workbench table is refused. No view-name column is added to masking_rule.
why: The legacy guardrail requires a rule to name a view column and no source gives masking_rule a column for the view or the column name, so the naming rule must be carried by the field id rather than by a new column.

text: The four schema shapes, their field names and their types are this revision's decision. MaskingProfile carries roleCode, fieldId, viewName, columnName, unmasked, maskingVersion, validFrom, validTo and dataAsOf; MaskingProfileRow carries roleCode, fieldId, viewName, columnName and unmasked; MaskingProfileVersion carries maskingVersion, validFrom, validTo, rowCount, authorReference, decisionRecordEntryRef and rows[]; MaskingProfilePage carries items[], page, size with a default of 50 and a maximum of 200, and total. The page shape follows RWB-P4-AD001-CON section 12.1, and masking_rule fixes only DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204.
why: No source defines an answer shape for a masking-profile read or write; masking_rule fixes seven columns and the same service already publishes a page of 50 by default and 200 at most.

impact: Medium: the shapes are consumed by the app story and the enforcement point on Day 1 and a later change is a major version.

text: The unmask request is the case reference and the field id, with the role code in the path. The unmask record names the case, the person key, the field id, the view and column, the masking version in force, the role code that carried the unmasked rule, the acting user reference and the time, and no clear value. The PII record itself is ACE Common's and is not redefined.
why: Legacy AC2 fixes only that the read is written to the PII log and no source fixes what the unmask request or its record carries; the record has to be buildable while the PII log's own shape stays with its owner.

text: The version in force is the masking version whose valid_from is the latest not after the date asked, one version answers whole, and the earlier version's valid_to closes on the day before a later valid_from. That is the dated-version rule this service already fixes for the role mapping in RWB-P4-AD001-CON BR6 and TSD P4 v3 T4 LOV-VERSION-STATUS, applied to masking_rule.
why: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 gives masking_rule valid_from and valid_to but no resolution rule, and legacy AC3 needs one version to be in force on a date.
